summary.text: David Taylor is the Republican U.S. Representative for Ohio's 2nd District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. An Ohio native who worked as an attorney in the Clermont County Prosecutor's Office and later as president of his family's business, he won the open seat in 2024. He serves on the Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Taylor was born in Ohio in 1969 and attended Amelia High School, according to his congressional biography. He earned a bachelor's degree from Miami University in 1992 and a law degree from the University of Dayton School of Law.

After law school he joined the Clermont County Prosecutor's Office, where his congressional biography says he tried criminal cases. He then returned to his family's business, Sardinia Ready Mix, Inc., where he served as president, according to his congressional biography and Ballotpedia.
Taylor won the open 2nd District seat in November 2024 (73.6% in the general election), succeeding Brad Wenstrup, and took office on January 3, 2025.

He serves on the House Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, where he is vice chairman of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee, and co-chairs the bipartisan Congressional Rural Broadband Caucus.
According to his congressional biography, Taylor lives in Clermont County with his wife, Charity; they have three daughters.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 64.2% of the vote to Jen Mazzuckelli's 35.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
